Any computer.
One command.

Carino Setup is one command that reads your machine and installs the drivers, codecs and software it needs.

  • A fresh install? It adds the repositories, codecs, firmware and the right graphics driver.
  • Setting a machine up for one job? Pick one of 15 purpose profiles, from gaming to medical imaging.
  • Not sure what it will change? A dry run prints every command and changes nothing.

Linux · Windows 10 and 11 · macOS 15 or newer · AGPL-3.0

Pick the machine you are setting up.

$ bash <(curl -s https://setup.carino.systems/setup.sh)

Fedora is what it is built and tested on. Debian, Ubuntu, Arch, openSUSE, RHEL and their derivatives are supported too, and Solus, Alpine, Void, Gentoo, Slackware and Mageia get the base packages, plus drivers where they are packaged (Gentoo and Slackware print the steps). Linux only: the BSDs are refused.

PS> iwr -useb https://setup.carino.systems/setup.ps1 | iex

Run Terminal as Administrator — the script stops without it. It prints what it found, installs the base apps and drivers with winget, applies the Windows 10 or 11 tweaks, offers the 15 purpose profiles and runs Windows Update.

Rehearse it first: $env:CARINO_SETUP_DRYRUN='1' before the command. Plans and the other options are under Available Arguments.

$ bash <(curl -s https://setup.carino.systems/macos.sh)

Run it as your normal user, not with sudo. It prints what it found, installs Homebrew and the base tools, offers the Finder tweaks and the 15 purpose profiles, then lists the macOS updates. macOS 15 or newer.

Rehearse it first: dry-run after the command. Plans and the other options are under Available Arguments.

This page runs entirely in your browser and sends nothing anywhere. The script is one readable file: setup.sh · setup.ps1 · macos.sh

What it does (and refuses)

What it does

  • Reads the machine before it touches it. Distribution family, CPU, every GPU and its NVIDIA generation, laptop or virtual machine, Secure Boot, free disk and internet, printed as a table before it asks anything.
  • Base packages and drivers that match. The repositories codecs and drivers need, a full upgrade, codecs, firmware and CPU microcode, then the GPU driver: the open NVIDIA module for Turing and newer, the 580 or 470 branch for older cards, Mesa for AMD and Intel, guest tools in a virtual machine.
  • 15 purpose profiles. Gaming, Corporate, Development, Design, Cybersecurity, Forensics, Scientific, Robotics, Medical Imaging and more — native packages and the Flatpaks that belong with them.
  • Twelve desktops, only when none is running. GNOME through Niri, where the family has a package list for them. The builder names the ones a family lacks and says why.
  • Carino Hyprland, if you want it. On Fedora 44 or newer it installs Atrium, the complete Hyprland desktop (bar, lock screen, launcher, notifications, settings, themes), with its own installer, which backs up your configuration first and offers to remove the desktop that was there (GNOME, KDE Plasma, COSMIC...) for a Hyprland-only machine. Atrium is made for Fedora 44 or newer only: on other distributions the script says so and points to the plain Hyprland desktop choice, which installs stock Hyprland where 0.55 or newer is available.
  • Windows and macOS too. setup.ps1 installs with winget and macos.sh with Homebrew: the same system table first, the same 15 purposes, Explorer or Finder tweaks and the system updates. Windows Update and the GPU vendor supply the Windows drivers; macOS ships its own.
  • Rehearses on request. A dry run prints every privileged command it would run and installs nothing.
  • One file you can audit. About a thousand lines of plain bash in numbered sections, with every package name kept together as data.

What it will not do

  • It is not a configuration manager. It installs once. It does not converge a machine to a described state, it does not run again on a schedule, and running it twice does not undo the first run. Ansible and Salt still have a job.
  • It is not sandboxed. It runs privileged commands, upgrades the whole system and adds third-party repositories — RPM Fusion, EPEL, Packman, Flathub, and the Hyprland COPR or PPA when you ask for Hyprland. Read the dry run before you run the real one.
  • It is not universal, and it says so. NixOS, Guix System, SteamOS, transactional openSUSE, the BSDs and anything it does not recognise are refused before anything runs, with the reason printed. On Gentoo it installs only the base packages, on Slackware the base packages, codecs and firmware, and it prints the rest as steps for you.
  • It is not a backup. Run it on a fresh install, not on a machine carrying work you have not copied off somewhere else.

Every distribution it knows

Fedora — Fedora, Nobara, Ultramarine, Risi. Fedora Atomic — Silverblue, Kinoite, Bazzite, Bluefin, Aurora, layered with rpm-ostree. Enterprise — RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, Oracle Linux, Amazon Linux.

Debian — Debian, LMDE, MX, Kali, Parrot, Devuan, Raspberry Pi OS. Ubuntu — Ubuntu and its flavours, Mint, Pop!_OS, elementary, Zorin, KDE neon, TUXEDO.

Arch — Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS, CachyOS, Garuda, ArcoLinux. openSUSE — Tumbleweed, Slowroll, Leap, SLES.

Base packages, plus drivers where they are packaged, with few or no purpose lists: Solus, Alpine, Void, Gentoo, Slackware, Mageia, OpenMandriva.

Carino Hyprland: Fedora 44 and newer only (Atrium). The plain Hyprland desktop: Fedora 44 and newer, Arch, openSUSE Tumbleweed and Slowroll, Debian 13 and newer (and derivatives built on them, such as LMDE 7), Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 bases (derivatives included), Ubuntu 26.10+ itself, Solus.

Refused, with the reason printed: NixOS, Guix System, SteamOS, MicroOS, Aeon, Kalpa and anything it does not recognise.

setup.sh is for Linux only. On FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD and DragonFly it stops and names the system's own tool (pkg, pkg_add, pkgin); on macOS it points to macos.sh. The BSDs do not ship bash by default, so install it first to see that message.

The Plan Builder shows what each family gets — pick the distribution there to read the one you came for.

Available Arguments

Flag Action
no argumentInteractive: checks the system, then the base setup, a desktop if none is running, purpose profiles and Carino Hyprland.
quickBase setup, then the Basic profile's native apps and the basic and Google Flatpaks.
simpleBase setup only: repositories, upgrade, base packages, codecs, firmware and drivers.
serverBase, server and development packages, then enables SSH and Cockpit.
drivers nvidia/amd/intelGPU drivers only. All four do the same: the GPU is detected.
desktopOpens the desktop menu, even when a desktop is already running.
hyprlandInstalls the Carino Hyprland desktop only: Atrium, for Fedora 44 and newer (elsewhere it says why not).
distroboxCreates Fedora, Ubuntu and Debian distrobox containers.
protonInstalls the latest GE-Proton for Steam, native or Flatpak.
librewolfInstalls LibreWolf: from its repository on Fedora, EL, Debian and Ubuntu, as a Flatpak elsewhere.
anydeskEnables Flathub and installs the AnyDesk and RustDesk flatpaks.
shareMounts a Windows/CIFS share at ~/WinFiles.
updateRefreshes and upgrades the packages and Flatpaks.
dry-runGoes before any argument: prints every system-changing command and changes nothing.
helpPrints the usage text.

CARINO_SETUP_PLAN

Comma-separated tokens, run left to right with no questions. One unknown token refuses the whole plan before anything runs.

Token Action
technicalBase setup, including the drivers, then the desktop menu, which takes none under a plan.
drivers update serverThe same as the arguments of the same name.
desktop=<name>One desktop: gnome xfce kde lxqt cinnamon mate i3 openbox budgie sway hyprland niri carino-hyprland none.
hyprlandThe same as desktop=carino-hyprland.
purpose=<name>One purpose profile, may repeat: basic gaming corporate corporate-microsoft corporate-google development astronomy compneuro design music cybersecurity forensics scientific robotics imagenology.
reboot=yes|noWhether to reboot at the end. Default: no.

Windows · macOS

setup.ps1 and macos.sh read a plan from the same variable; the Linux arguments above do not apply to them. Tokens run left to right, and one unknown token refuses the whole plan before anything runs.

PS> $env:CARINO_SETUP_PLAN='technical,tweaks,purpose=gaming'; iwr -useb https://setup.carino.systems/setup.ps1 | iex
$ CARINO_SETUP_PLAN=technical,tweaks,purpose=design bash <(curl -s https://setup.carino.systems/macos.sh)
Token Action
technicalWindows: base apps, Visual C++ runtimes and drivers with winget. macOS: Command Line Tools, Homebrew and the base tools.
tweaksWindows: dark apps, file extensions and a cleaner taskbar. macOS: file extensions, the Finder path bar, no .DS_Store on network drives and a screenshots folder.
updateWindows: upgrades every winget app, then Windows Update. macOS: brew upgrade, then the macOS updates.
drivers wslWindows only: the drivers step alone, and WSL with Ubuntu.
purpose=<name> reboot=yes|noThe same names and defaults as on Linux.
CARINO_SETUP_DRYRUN=1Prints every system-changing command and changes nothing. On macOS, dry-run after the command does the same.
